newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan firm to build science-park power plant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan firm to build science-park power plant.

text.p: Taiwan's Asia Pacific Energy Development Co said on Wednesday it would build an LNG-powered power station by 1998 to ease shortages at the Hsinchu Science Park, the island's high-technology centre.
Construction on the T$4.5 billion power station will start in early 1997 with delivery of power targeted for late 1998, a company official said by telephone.
Powered by liquefied natural gas, the plant is designed with maximum generating capacity of 150,000 megawatts, he said.
Taiwan energy experts estimated a power station of that size would consume 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes of LNG a year.

Output value of the Hsinchu Science Park reached T$280 billion in 1995, but power outages and surges caused by erratic power supplies are a real threat to manufacturing and research systems used by the park's high-tech tenants.
